how: claude.ai website; Sonnet 5, medium effort (default); memory off; a new chat per case, instruction pasted above the question

cases.answer:
RECOMMENDED: Species: Human; Genome assembly: GRCh38; Input file format: VCF; Transcript database: Ensembl/GENCODE basic; Gene symbol; Pathogenicity predictions: SIFT, PolyPhen; Frequency data: gnomAD (exomes + genomes) allele frequencies; ClinVar phenotype annotations; RegulatoryBuild (regulatory region annotation); Non-coding/regulatory consequences (include intergenic, upstream/downstream, TFBS annotations)
* OPTIONAL: CADD/REVEL plugin scores; UTRAnnotator; Existing variant/co-located variants; Transcript Function/GO annotations; Protein domains (Pfam/Interpro); HGVS notation; TSL/APPRIS annotations; Nearest gene for intergenic variants
* NOT ON THE FORM: Splice-impact deep learning predictors (e.g., SpliceAI, CADD-splice) beyond what's available as installed plugins — these require separate plugin installation, not a form tick; long-read/structural variant handling (form is for small variants only, as you've indicated); functional wet-lab validation
* ASSUMED: You are using the online web interface (not the CLI/API) and can access plugin-supported options; assumed GRCh38 as your reference build (specify if GRCh37); assumed you want gnomAD as your population frequency source (specify if you need a different/regional reference panel); assumed input is already in VCF format from your WGS pipeline

RECOMMENDED: Species: Human; Input file format: VCF; Transcript database: Ensembl/GENCODE transcripts; Gene symbol; Biotype; ClinVar / Phenotypes, diseases and traits; Regulatory build (identify regulatory features); Existing variants (co-located known variants for population ID matching); Frequency data from gnomAD (genomes); Pathogenicity predictions (SIFT, PolyPhen-2); REVEL/CADD (pathogenicity/impact scores)
OPTIONAL: Identify overlapping structural variants; TSL/APPRIS/MANE Select transcript annotations; HGVS notation; Exon/Intron numbers; Gene/protein domains (e.g. Pfam, InterPro); Non-synonymous filtering; miRNA/UTR annotations
NOT ON THE FORM: De novo structural variant calling/detection itself (VEP annotates SVs already present as calls in the input, e.g. from a VCF; it does not call or discover SVs from raw WGS reads) — this must be done upstream with a dedicated SV caller before submission
ASSUMED: Input is already variant-called (a VCF of SNVs/indels and, separately, structural variant calls) rather than raw sequencing reads, since VEP requires pre-called variants as input; genome build assumed GRCh38 unless the researcher specifies GRCh37

RECOMMENDED: Species/assembly = Human GRCh38; Input format = VCF (structural variant/CNV encoded with SVTYPE and END/SVLEN); Transcript/gene set = Ensembl/GENCODE (default); Regulatory build – "Show regulatory region consequences"; Gene symbol (Identifiers); Transcript biotype; Pick one consequence per gene / "Most severe consequence" summary option, so coding and regulatory hits across many overlapped features are easy to scan
* OPTIONAL: RefSeq or "Ensembl+RefSeq" transcript set as a cross-check; ClinVar phenotype annotation; gnomAD-SV frequency annotation (if offered as a plugin/data source) for filtering common CNVs; "Show overlap" / proportion of transcript or regulatory feature overlapped by the SV, where the web form exposes it; downstream/upstream distance option if you also want nearby gene effects flagged
* NOT ON THE FORM: CNV pathogenicity/dosage-sensitivity scoring (e.g., haploinsufficiency/triplosensitivity scores, ACMG-style CNV classification) — VEP reports consequence terms only, not clinical impact calls; precise breakpoint-level functional modeling (e.g., disrupted TAD/enhancer-promoter looping) beyond simple overlap with annotated regulatory features
* ASSUMED: Genome build GRCh38; variants are supplied as a VCF (or equivalent) with proper SV/CNV representation (SVTYPE, END/SVLEN fields) rather than as plain SNV-style rows; "quickly identify" means a summarized, one-line-per-variant consequence view is preferred over full per-transcript detail

RECOMMENDED: Species = Human; Assembly = GRCh38 (or GRCh37 if that's your cohort's build); Input format = VCF; "Regulatory build" (include overlapping regulatory features, under Annotations & Predictions) to get consequence terms for regulatory regions; "Frequency data for co-located variants" (include gnomAD and 1000 Genomes population allele frequencies)
OPTIONAL: TOPMed frequencies (additional population reference for rare-variant filtering); "Pick" or "Flag pick" (one representative annotation per variant, useful if output volume is large); Gene/transcript biotype filters if you want to narrow output further after the run
NOT ON THE FORM: A single checkbox to restrict the run to "regulatory-region-overlapping SVs only" — the form annotates all overlaps (coding, regulatory, intergenic, etc.) and doesn't let you filter to just regulatory hits before running; you'll need to filter the output afterward (e.g. by consequence terms such as regulatory_region_variant, TF_binding_site_variant). Also note: structural variant frequency annotation depends on overlap with known SVs in the reference databases (e.g. gnomAD-SV, 1000 Genomes SV, DGV) rather than exact allele matching as with SNVs — the form does not compute novel population frequencies for SVs it hasn't seen before.
ASSUMED: Genome assembly not stated (defaulted recommendation to GRCh38); input file is in VCF format with structural variants encoded via SVTYPE/END or similar; "common in the general population" refers to standard population reference databases (gnomAD/1000 Genomes) rather than a specific custom cohort.

RECOMMENDED: Species = Human (Homo sapiens); Genome assembly = GRCh38; Input format = VCF; Transcript database = Ensembl/GENCODE transcripts; "Find co-located known variants" (dbSNP/ClinVar); Frequency data for co-located variants — gnomAD exomes/genomes and 1000 Genomes; ClinVar clinical significance annotation; SIFT; PolyPhen-2; Gene/transcript identifiers (Gene symbol, HGNC); structural variant overlap annotation (transcript-overlapping SVs, so CNV/SV breakpoints get gene/consequence calls)
OPTIONAL: CADD plugin (if enabled on the instance); REVEL plugin; Regulatory build consequences (for non-coding/regulatory overlap of SVs); Nearest gene annotation (for intergenic SV breakpoints); COSMIC known-variant identifiers
NOT ON THE FORM: CNV calling/copy-number quantification itself (VEP only annotates overlap of already-called SVs/CNVs with genes/transcripts, it does not detect or size CNVs); somatic-specific actionability/tiering databases (e.g., OncoKB, CIViC) — not available as VEP web options
ASSUMED: Genome build is GRCh38; input is already in VCF format with SVs represented via standard SV VCF conventions (SVTYPE/END/etc.); "clinical pathogenicity" refers to ClinVar annotations rather than a bespoke somatic actionability score; population frequency reference of interest is gnomAD/1000 Genomes rather than a disease-specific cohort

RECOMMENDED: Species = Human; Identify input format (or Auto-detect); Structural variant overlap; Regulatory build (Regulatory features); Frequency data for co-located variants (1000 Genomes / gnomAD population frequencies); Show co-located known variants
OPTIONAL: gnomAD exomes/genomes frequency filtering options; TSL (Transcript Support Level); Gene Ontology / phenotype annotations; RefSeq/GENCODE transcript set choice; Interpro domains; nearest gene for intergenic variants
NOT ON THE FORM: none
ASSUMED: input is a list of structural variant coordinates (e.g. VCF with SVTYPE/END or BED-style CNV calls) rather than SNVs; "healthy people" population frequency refers to the general population reference cohorts (e.g. gnomAD-SV) built into VEP, not a user-supplied matched control cohort

RECOMMENDED: Species = Mouse (Mus musculus, GRCm39); Input format = VCF; "Restrict results" / filter to coding consequences (missense_variant, stop_gained, stop_lost, frameshift_variant, inframe_insertion/deletion, etc.); SIFT (pathogenicity prediction — available for mouse); Gene symbol / identifiers annotation; Protein domains and features
OPTIONAL: Exon/intron numbers; Transcript support level / biotype filter (to restrict to protein_coding transcripts); Regulatory region annotations; "Pick one consequence per variant" (for a simplified summary output)
NOT ON THE FORM: PolyPhen-2 — this predictor is human-only in Ensembl VEP and is not offered for Mus musculus, so functional pathogenicity here can only be scored with SIFT (not PolyPhen); VEP also has no option to confirm/filter variants by "germline" status — that filtering must be done upstream in your variant calling, not on this form
ASSUMED: Variants are supplied as a VCF file; reference assembly is GRCm39 (current mouse build); you are using the Ensembl web VEP interface rather than the command-line/API tool; "coding regions" means protein_coding transcript biotype rather than a custom BED-restricted region

RECOMMENDED: Species = Danio rerio (zebrafish); Input file format = VCF; Transcript database = Ensembl/GENCODE (default Ensembl transcripts); "Gene symbol" (identifiers); "Consequence" annotations (per-transcript consequence, e35.g. missense_variant, frameshift_variant, stop_gained); "Protein" (show protein position/amino acid change, HGVSp notation); "SIFT" (predicted deleteriousness of missense changes, available for zebrafish); "Restrict to protein-coding transcripts" filter
OPTIONAL: "HGVS" notation (HGVSc/HGVSp for reporting); "Exon/Intron numbers"; "Existing variants" (co-located known variants, if a zebrafish variation database is available); "Regulatory features" (only if you also want non-coding context); "Filter by consequence type" (e.g. restrict output to missense/LoF only, useful for driver prioritization); "Gene Ontology/pathway annotations" if available for zebrafish in VEP plugins
NOT ON THE FORM: PolyPhen-2 scores (human-only predictor, not available for zebrafish); dedicated "somatic driver mutation" or cancer-driver pathogenicity classification (VEP annotates functional consequence/predicted impact only, it does not determine tumor-driver status or perform cohort-level significance/recurrence analysis — that requires downstream tools, e.g. dNdScv, OncodriveFML, MutSigCV); direct tumor-vs-germline somatic-status calling (must already be done upstream of VEP)
ASSUMED: Variants are already called and available as a standard variant file (e.g. VCF) with genomic coordinates on a current zebrafish reference assembly; you want per-variant transcript/protein consequence annotation rather than only whole-cohort summary statistics

RECOMMENDED: Species = Mouse (Mus musculus, GRCm39); Input format = VCF; Transcript set = Ensembl transcripts (default); "Find overlapping regulatory features" (regulatory build annotation) — ticked, since this is the option that flags enhancers/promoters/CTCF/TF-binding sites overlapping your variants; leave default consequence/transcript annotation on, since intergenic/upstream/downstream/intronic consequence calls are how VEP flags non-coding location
OPTIONAL: "Pick one consequence per variant" (simplifies output for a quick top-line scan rather than all overlapping transcripts/features); adjusting the upstream/downstream distance parameter if your enhancers of interest lie beyond the default 5kb window; gene symbol/identifier annotation if you want gene context for nearby regulatory hits; "show frequency data" is not informative here since this is a novel WGS cohort, so skip population frequency options
NOT ON THE FORM: quantitative non-coding functional impact scores (e.g., CADD, DeepSEA, motif-disruption/TF-binding-affinity scores) — these rely on plugins that are largely human-only and not available/validated for mouse; "regulatory feature overlap" only tells you that a variant falls in an annotated feature, not a predicted functional consequence score for that overlap
ASSUMED: your data is in VCF format; you are using the current mouse reference assembly (GRCm39) in Ensembl; "wild-type" cohort means no additional case/control or somatic filtering is needed; you want a single annotation run rather than a phased/family-based analysis

RECOMMENDED: Species: Danio_rerio; Input file format: VCF; Transcript database: Ensembl/GENCODE transcripts; RegulatoryBuild - Regulatory features; Consequence type filter (to surface regulatory_region_variant/TF_binding_site_variant); Existing variants (identify known co-located variants)
OPTIONAL: Overlapping SVs (if any larger somatic rearrangements are present); Frequency data / gnomAD-style co-located variant frequencies (if available for zebrafish); Gene phenotype annotations; TSL/appris annotations (transcript support metrics, if evaluating nearby transcripts); Downstream/upstream distance customization for regulatory context
NOT ON THE FORM: dedicated transcription-factor-binding-motif disruption scoring (e.g., motif gain/loss prediction akin to human-focused plugins) — VEP's regulatory build annotation flags overlap with regulatory features/TF binding sites but does not itself score binding-site disruption pathogenicity; this typically requires an external motif-analysis tool
ASSUMED: You are using the Ensembl zebrafish (Danio_rerio) reference assembly and gene/regulatory build that matches your variant coordinates; variants are already called and formatted as VCF; "non-coding" here means intergenic/regulatory rather than intronic-only

RECOMMENDED: Species = Mouse (select correct assembly, e.g. GRCm39); Input format = VCF; "Regulatory build" (include regulatory feature and motif consequence annotations); "Show nearest gene(s)" (for intergenic/non-coding hits); Gene symbol identifier annotation
OPTIONAL: Transcript set choice (Ensembl vs RefSeq, if offered for mouse); “Distance to transcript” cutoff adjustment for intergenic classification; TSL/APPRIS-style transcript flags if available for mouse; conservation scores if listed for this species
NOT ON THE FORM: SIFT and PolyPhen-2 predictions (human-only, not computed for mouse); population frequency annotations like gnomAD/1000 Genomes (human-only); dedicated non-coding pathogenicity scores such as CADD, DANN, or FATHMM-MKL (VEP web form does not provide these for any species, and none exist for mouse) — VEP will annotate consequence/location, not a pathogenicity score
ASSUMED: Data is in VCF format; genome assembly is GRCm39 (current mouse reference); "regulatory and non-coding" includes intergenic, intronic, and regulatory-build-annotated regions rather than a custom-defined region set

RECOMMENDED: Species = Mouse (Mus musculus); consequence type annotation (default, includes coding and regulatory consequence categorization); Gene symbol; Biotype (to distinguish protein-coding vs non-coding transcripts); Regulatory build annotation (to flag regulatory/non-coding region overlap)
OPTIONAL: SIFT; PolyPhen (mouse PolyPhen support is limited — check availability); Identify canonical transcripts; Protein domains; Existing variants (co-located known variants); TSL/APPRIS annotations; Gene Ontology terms; Pathway annotation
NOT ON THE FORM: driver-gene prioritization/ranking, somatic vs germline filtering or calling, and cross-referencing against known cancer driver databases (e.g., COSMIC/IntOGen) — VEP annotates consequence only, it does not classify "driver" status
ASSUMED: Input coordinates are on a recent mouse reference assembly (e.g., GRCm39) consistent between WES and WGS callsets; variants are already called and provided as VCF or similar standard format; no assumption made about whether phasing or transcript-set (RefSeq vs Ensembl) preference is needed, so default transcript set was assumed

RECOMMENDED: Phenotype data (annotate with known variant/gene-disease associations)
OPTIONAL: Gene symbol; RefSeq transcripts; Filtering options (post-run) to restrict output to genes of interest; Frequency data (gnomAD) if prioritizing by rarity; Pick one consequence per variant (if a simplified summary is wanted)
NOT ON THE FORM: VEP cannot search for or discover variants based on a disease/gene association — it only annotates variants you already supply (as VCF, HGVS, etc.). Identifying "variants in genes associated with colorectal cancer" requires you to first obtain a variant call set (e.g., from your own sequencing data or a public variant database) and a list of colorectal-cancer-associated genes (e.g., from a resource like COSMIC, OMIM, or a curated panel); VEP can then only be used afterward to annotate/filter that pre-existing variant list.
ASSUMED: That you already have (or can obtain) a set of called variants to upload, since VEP requires variant input rather than performing variant discovery itself.

RECOMMENDED: Gene symbol; Phenotypes (include known phenotype-associated variants/genes); Co-located known variants (dbSNP/ClinVar identifiers)
OPTIONAL: SIFT; PolyPhen; gnomAD frequencies; Consequence-based filtering (e.g. restrict to missense/LoF variants) applied after VEP output
NOT ON THE FORM: A built-in filter restricting output to only genes/variants "associated with breast cancer" — VEP will annotate phenotype/disease associations genome-wide, but selecting or filtering specifically for breast cancer genes is not a form option; this would need to be done by post-filtering the results (e.g. against a gene list such as BRCA1/BRCA2 or a panel).
ASSUMED: Input file is in VCF format; genome build and species not specified (assumed human, most recent GRCh38 assembly); "sample" implies a multi-sample VCF but no genotype-based filtering was requested.

RECOMMENDED: Species = Human (assumed); Identifiers: Gene Symbol; Identifiers: Transcript version; Consequence type annotations (default "Basic options" - Ensembl transcripts)
OPTIONAL: RefSeq transcripts (if clinical-style reporting preferred); Protein domains; ClinVar/Phenotype annotations; Pathogenicity predictions (SIFT/PolyPhen); Conservation scores
NOT ON THE FORM: Restricting the VEP run itself to only BRCA1/BRCA2 — VEP annotates whatever variants you submit; it does not have a submission-time "gene of interest" filter. You must either (a) supply an input file already limited to variants in these genes, or (b) run VEP normally and filter the output table by Gene Symbol afterward.
ASSUMED: Species is human; input will be a VCF or list of variant identifiers (not just gene names) since VEP requires variant-level input, not gene-level input; genome assembly (GRCh38) not specified.

RECOMMENDED: LOFTEE plugin (loss-of-function transcript effect confidence); Gene symbol; Consequence type filter (set to "Show only variants with these consequences" and select high-impact terms like stop_gained, frameshift_variant, splice_donor_variant, splice_acceptor_variant, start_lost, stop_lost); Identify variants: existing known variants (dbSNP/ClinVar); Pick one consequence per gene
OPTIONAL: gnomAD/1000 Genomes frequency annotation (to flag rare vs common variants); ClinVar clinical significance; Protein domains (e.g. Pfam/PROSITE) for context on truncated regions; RefSeq transcript set as an alternative/addition to Ensembl transcripts if your panel is annotated against RefSeq
NOT ON THE FORM: restricting the analysis to a custom gene panel list directly (the form does not accept a gene list upload for pre-filtering; you must run all variants and filter output by gene symbol afterward, or restrict your input VCF to panel regions before uploading)
ASSUMED: you are uploading a VCF or list of variant coordinates covering your panel genes (not raw sequencing reads); your genome build is one of GRCh37/GRCh38 (not specified which); "loss-of-function" is intended in the LOFTEE/PTV sense (stop-gained, frameshift, essential splice site) rather than including missense variants with predicted functional loss

RECOMMENDED: Species = Human; Regulatory build (include overlaps with regulatory regions); Motif features (transcription factor binding motifs); Restrict results by consequence type → filter to regulatory_region_variant, TF_binding_site_variant, TFBS_ablation/amplification, regulatory_region_ablation/amplification, intergenic_variant
OPTIONAL: Nearest gene/feature annotation (to see what regulatory element sits near); Frequency data filters (e.g. gnomAD) if they later want to prioritise rare regulatory hits; Pick one consequence per variant (simplifies "what each one hits" output)
NOT ON THE FORM: A dedicated "non-coding regulatory only" input mode — VEP annotates all overlapping consequences and you filter/restrict the output afterward rather than excluding coding regions upfront; none of the checkboxes actually determine "regulatory" biological function, only whether known regulatory build/motif annotations are checked
ASSUMED: Genome build GRCh38; input format is VCF or a standard variant list; "constitutional" means germline single-sample calls, no somatic/tumour-normal filtering needed

RECOMMENDED: Species = Homo sapiens; Include regulatory feature annotation (to flag promoter/enhancer overlap); Include frequency data for co-located variants; tick population frequency sources (1000 Genomes/gnomAD) under that option; leave "Co-located variants" checked (default) so known frequencies attach to your SNVs and indels
OPTIONAL: Restrict to specific populations of interest (e.g. gnomAD subpopulations) if you only care about certain groups; add custom annotation track for curated enhancer databases (e.g. FANTOM5) if regulatory build alone isn't granular enough; "pick worst consequence per gene" or "most severe consequence" display filters if output gets large
NOT ON THE FORM: distinguishing "inherited from parents" (trio/segregation analysis) — VEP annotates individual variants only and has no pedigree/inheritance-tracking option
ASSUMED: genome assembly GRCh38; you want standard 1000 Genomes/gnomAD population labels rather than a custom/local frequency panel; "somatic" flag left off since these are described as germline/inherited variants

RECOMMENDED: Species = Sus scrofa (pig); Input format = VCF (or VEP default format with chromosome/position/alleles); Transcript/gene consequence annotation (default); SIFT (under "Predictions" section) — this is the deleteriousness score available for pig
OPTIONAL: "Identify overlapping protein domains"; "Find co-located known variants" (if a pig variation database is available in the cache); restricting/filtering output to missense_variant consequence only, to simplify review of results; gene symbol/transcript identifier annotations for interpreting hits
NOT ON THE FORM: PolyPhen — this predictor is human-only and cannot be applied to pig variants, so no PolyPhen-based deleteriousness score will be produced
ASSUMED: Variant positions are given as genomic coordinates relative to a standard Sus scrofa reference assembly compatible with Ensembl's pig annotation/cache, and that a SIFT model has been precomputed for pig in the VEP cache being used

RECOMMENDED: Species = Sheep (Ovis aries); Identify known variants (co-located variants) — to flag any that already exist in Ensembl Variation for sheep
OPTIONAL: Show frequency data (only useful if population frequency annotation happens to exist for sheep variants in Ensembl Variation — coverage is likely sparse compared to human)
NOT ON THE FORM: Calculating how common each variant is across your breeds — VEP annotates and cross-references single variants against existing databases, it does not compute allele frequencies from your own multi-breed genotype/VCF data. You'd need a separate cohort tool (e.g., vcftools, PLINK, bcftools +fill-tags) run per breed group to get that.
ASSUMED: Variants are supplied as VCF (or similarly standard VEP input format) with genotype calls per sample/breed available in your own files, not in the VEP output itself
